newsitem.title: JORDAN: Hamas calls for release of Islamists in Jordan.
newsitem.headline: Hamas calls for release of Islamists in Jordan.

text.p: The Islamic resistance movement Hamas urged the Jordanian government on Thursday to release 10 Islamists it said were detained this month.

Hamas spokesman Ibrahim Ghosheh said the men, including a newspaper editor, a university teacher, a student and the head of a hospital nursing department, were detained by security officials in the last 10 days.

A Hamas source said on Wednesday the men were all supporters of the movement and one of them, general manager of the London based Islamist magazine Moslem Palestine Abdel-Aziz al-Amri, was a Hamas politburo member.

"We were astonished that the government of Jordan put these people in jail, especially Abdel-Aziz al-Amri...at the same time when Palestinian people are confronting the Israeli army," Ghosheh said in reference to two days of running battles between Israelis and Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza.
More than 30 people have been killed in the fighting, sparked by Israel's opening of a tunnel close to a Moslem sanctuary in Jerusalem.
"We ask the government to release these Islamists as soon as possible to allow Palestinians on the outside to support the cause," Ghosheh said.
Jordan signed a peace treaty two years ago with Israel and has come under pressure from both the Jewish state and Palestinian authorities to shut down any Hamas activity on its territory.
